blocks.headline: Am Flughafen
blocks.bodyGerman:
Guten Tag! Ich heiße Thomas Müller. Wie heißen Sie?

Guten Tag! Ich heiße Alex und ich komme aus Indien.

Freut mich, Sie kennenzulernen!
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Good day! My name is Thomas Müller. What's your name?

Good day! My name is Alex and I come from India.

Pleased to meet you!

blocks.title: Du oder Sie?
blocks.bodyEnglish: Capitalized 'Sie' is the formal you. 'du' is for friends, family and children. First meetings with adults use 'Sie' until you are invited to use 'du' — being offered the first name is the signal.

blocks.title: Handschlag oder Küsschen?
blocks.bodyEnglish: A firm handshake is the default greeting almost everywhere, including on meeting someone for the first time. Cheek kisses are for people you already know well, and mostly in the south. When in doubt: handshake, and stand a little closer than you would in English.

blocks.headline: Die Kernwörter
blocks.bodyEnglish: The five words that carry every first conversation.

blocks.headline: Sie vs du
blocks.bodyEnglish: German has two 'you'. Formal 'Sie' (always capitalized!) takes verb + -en like they: 'Wie heißen Sie?' — 'wohnen Sie'. Informal 'du' takes -st / -t: 'Wie heißt du?' — 'wohnst du'.

blocks.headline: Sich verabschieden
blocks.bodyEnglish: 'Auf Wiedersehen' is the safe formal goodbye anywhere. 'Tschüss' is casual — friends and family only. In the south you'll also hear 'Servus' for both hello and goodbye.

blocks.title: Sich vorstellen
blocks.formula: Ich heiße + [Name] + und ich komme aus + [Land/Stadt].
blocks.explanationEnglish: The standard self-introduction. The 'und' joins two full clauses — each keeps its own verb position.

examples.german: Ich heiße Lukas und ich komme aus Wien.
examples.english: My name is Lukas and I come from Vienna.

examples.german: Ich heiße Anna und ich komme aus Berlin.
examples.english: My name is Anna and I come from Berlin.

blocks.title: Nachfragen (formal)
blocks.explanationEnglish: W-question word first, verb second — the V2 skeleton you'll meet in section 2.
'Ich heiße …' introduces your name. 'komme' needs 'aus', 'wohnen' needs a place.

blocks.prompt: Which goodbye fits a job interview?
blocks.explanationEnglish: Formal setting = 'Auf Wiedersehen'. 'Tschüss' and 'Servus' are casual.
Stranger + formal = 'Wie heißen Sie?' — note the capital S.

blocks.title: Was du jetzt kannst
bullets: Vorstellen: Ich heiße … und ich komme aus …
Formal fragen: Wie heißen Sie? — Woher kommen Sie?
Sie vs du: mit Erwachsenen erst 'Sie', bis du angeboten wird.
